obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems must establish and document a quality management system that ensures regulatory compliance, covering at least strategy, design, development, testing, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, incident reporting, communications, record-keeping, resource management, and accountability frameworks.
exceptions: Providers subject to quality management obligations under relevant sectoral Union law may integrate the required aspects into those existing systems (paragraph 3).

Financial institution providers subject to internal governance requirements under Union financial services law are deemed compliant with the quality management system obligation (except for risk management, post-market monitoring, and serious incident reporting requirements) by complying with those internal governance rules (paragraph 4).

obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems must implement the quality management system in a manner proportionate to the size of their organisation while maintaining the degree of rigour and level of protection required to ensure compliance with this Regulation.

Providers of high-risk AI systems already subject to quality management obligations under relevant sectoral Union law may incorporate the required quality management aspects into those existing sectoral quality management systems rather than creating a separate system.

Providers that are financial institutions subject to Union financial services law internal governance requirements must take into account any relevant harmonised standards when fulfilling their quality management obligations through those internal governance arrangements.
exceptions: The deemed-compliance exemption for financial institutions does not extend to the risk management system (Article 9), post-market monitoring system (Article 72), or serious incident reporting procedures (Article 73), which must still be fulfilled separately.
